title: Evaluate Muse Spark 1.1 for governed model routing
description: Build an isolated Meta Model API adapter and reproducible benchmark to decide whether Muse Spark 1.1 should be rejected, bounded, or promoted for scoped routing.
pain_point: Vendor claims and API policy are unverified, so promotion cannot be justified without correctness, safety, privacy, reliability, and cost evidence.
use_case: Compare Muse with existing model lanes on fixed governed-agent tasks and record a disposition.

pre_hitl_prediction.title: 建立Muse Spark 1.1适配器与可重复跨模型基准测试包
pre_hitl_prediction.description: 需要构建一个Meta Model API适配器和一个可重复的跨模型基准测试包，以评估Muse Spark 1.1模型是否应被路由到生产工作流中。评估必须通过正确性、安全性、隐私、延迟、可靠性和治理门控，并基于成本效益比较多个模型（如GPT-5.6系列、Claude Fable 5等），最终确定拒绝、限制使用或推广的处置。
pre_hitl_prediction.pain_point: 目前缺乏一个系统化、可重复的评估框架来客观衡量Muse Spark 1.1是否满足生产级门控条件，导致无法做出路由推广或拒绝的决策，且现有流程中容易混入供应商声明、第三方证据和本地观测，需要严格分离信息源以避免误导。
pre_hitl_prediction.use_case: 开发团队需要决定是否将Muse Spark 1.1加入模型路由栈，因此需要构建适配器和基准测试包，在MCP可靠性、受控委托、仓库执行、长上下文完整性、计算机使用安全、成本调整正确性等维度上运行相同任务，并与现有模型比较，收集通过率、成本、延迟、重试等数据，以支持正式决策。

title: Maintain a compact exact-latest review inbox
description: Keep the latest HVAC review notes short, exact, and accompanied by page and environment context before an agent acts.
pain_point: Long inboxes can truncate and prevent ChatGPT or Codex from reading the complete latest note.
use_case: Route current HVAC review feedback to an agent while preserving the exact note and its source page.

pre_hitl_prediction.title: Keep notes short enough for ChatGPT/Codex to read full text
pre_hitl_prediction.description: Users need HVAC review notes to be concise so that AI tools like ChatGPT or Codex can read the entire text without truncation, ensuring full context is preserved before any agent action.
pre_hitl_prediction.pain_point: Notes that are too long get truncated by AI tools, causing loss of exact latest note text and missing context from page label, route, URL, viewport, user agent, priority, kind, and visible context.
pre_hitl_prediction.use_case: In the HVAC review inbox, ensuring each latest note is brief enough to be read entirely by ChatGPT or Codex tooling, preserving the exact note text and attached metadata before any agent acts.

title: Preview generated documents without syncing scratch artifacts
description: Provide a first-party way to inspect generated document artifacts while rejecting invalid no-sync arguments and keeping temporary previews out of project sync.
pain_point: No first-party way to look at a generated PDF; the agent had to manually rasterize and read images, wasting additional sandbox round-trips. Also, `--no-sync-output` silently accepted a path argument and discarded the needed files, forcing a re-run. Scratch preview artifacts auto-synced into the project and required manual cleanup locally and remotely.
use_case: Generate a PDF in a sandbox and visually verify it before completing the task.

pre_hitl_prediction.title: First-party way to view sandbox-generated PDF artifacts
pre_hitl_prediction.description: The CLI lacks a built-in command to view generated PDFs (or other document artifacts) from sandbox runs. The agent had to manually rasterize the PDF to PNG using a second sandbox invocation and then read each image, repeating this cycle after fixes. This adds friction and extra round-trips for every sandbox-generated document.
pre_hitl_prediction.pain_point: No first-party way to look at a generated PDF; the agent had to manually rasterize and read images, wasting additional sandbox round-trips. Also, `--no-sync-output` silently accepted a path argument and discarded the needed files, forcing a re-run. Scratch preview artifacts auto-synced into the project and required manual cleanup locally and remotely.
pre_hitl_prediction.use_case: User ran a one-off data task (CSV in, PDF report out) via `gipity sandbox run`. The agent needed to visually confirm the PDF layout before calling the task done. It had to hand-roll a second sandbox invocation running `pdftoppm -png -r 90 docs/sales-report.pdf docs/preview` to rasterize pages, then use `Read` on each PNG. After a chart fix, the rasterize-and-read cycle was repeated.

pre_hitl_prediction.title: Push notification for queue execution summaries
pre_hitl_prediction.description: Each queue execution should post a summary comment so that Alex gets a push notification via the GitHub app.
pre_hitl_prediction.pain_point: Without automatic posting of summary comments, Alex would not get push notifications and would miss real-time updates on queue execution status.
pre_hitl_prediction.use_case: Alex receives push notifications on GitHub app for each queue execution's summary comment in the pinned tracking issue, enabling real-time monitoring of the autonomous crank loop.

title: Deterministic game loop stepping in page eval for physics/animation verification
description: Provide a platform path to advance a running game loop deterministically so agents can verify physics and animation behavior in a headless browser.
pain_point: Wall-clock waits run the page too slowly and can produce false negatives, while the CLI warning recommends deterministic stepping that the platform does not expose.
use_case: Verify ball movement, collisions, scoring, and lives in a Phaser game before shipping it.

pre_hitl_prediction.title: Deterministic game loop stepping in page eval for physics/animation verification
pre_hitl_prediction.description: The platform's `page eval` tool cannot run a canvas render loop at sufficient speed for verification. When the agent attempted to verify a Phaser brick-breaker game's real-time gameplay loop (ball bounces, bricks break, score increments, lives decrement), the page painted at 14.5 fps and the platform warned that waiting on wall-clock time advances physics far slower than it appears, recommending to 'step the app's own loop deterministically'. However, neither the CLI nor the platform provides any mechanism to step a running game loop deterministically. The agent had no follow-up move and abandoned real-time verification, shipping the game with its core mechanics never exercised. A tool or method is needed to step the application's animation/game loop in a deterministic, controllable way to enable reliable headless verification of physics, animations, and game state transitions.
pre_hitl_prediction.pain_point: The platform warns the agent to 'step the app's own loop deterministically' but provides no tool or method to do so. The agent had no follow-up move: it dropped real-time verification entirely, took a static screenshot, and shipped the game with its core mechanic (brick collision -> score -> win/lose transitions) never exercised. The verify step is the only step with no working tool for canvas/physics/animation apps.
pre_hitl_prediction.use_case: Agent built a Phaser brick-breaker game and tried to verify the real gameplay loop (ball bounces, bricks break, score increments, lives decrement) by driving the deployed page with `gipity page eval`. The first two evals worked (sampled ball position over time), but the third eval (which would confirm a brick collision and score change) received a warning that the page painted at 14.5 fps, that waiting on wall-clock time advances physics too slowly, and that the agent should instead 'step the app's own loop deterministically'. The agent had no way to do that, dropped real-time verification, took a static screenshot, and shipped the game with its core mechanic never exercised.
